note: Runbook v4 §3.5.3a detectability check on the merged PMT readout (dark counts off). The geometry is read from LUCiD's own config/WCTE_geom_config.json at the pinned revision; local tests use the schema-identical synthetic fixture from jepa_noise.lucid_bombs.from_synthetic. No LUCiD import, nothing redistributed. Every number is development-only; the 2026-10-17 frozen yields, F2-vs-F2' and s_p are superseded_pending_merged_readout and the author has not frozen replacements.
f3_marginalised_note: F3 is a random per-PMT gain, not known: s_p^2 * mu_p^2 is added to every PMT variance (the §3.5.6 mae_chi2 covariance term). s_p is the spread in force (lb.F3_SPREAD = 0.10), not the candidate spread of an F3 ceiling scan.

fixed_response.module_index: dense mPMT module index: response_manifest.module_groups(mpmt_id) over the sparse WCTE ids (0..105 with id 45 absent)
fixed_response.use_here: the charge gain multiplies mu_p in every ceiling (detector response, present in the nominal twin too)

previous_decision.use: read-only input: the previously frozen ceilings are recorded beside the new ones so the Lead can report them side by side

items: Y_lo, Y_hi (frozen 2026-10-17 on the pre-merge readout)
superseded_decisions.refreeze_condition: this check re-run on the merged readout; the author freezes the new values

geometry.note: id 45 absent; pmt_id_in_mpmt is 1-based; the host reads the npz, never a LUCiD import.

acceptance.note: Every factor used by a registered criterion needs a run-level ceiling >= 0.6 at the median yield. F1 cells below 0.6 stay in the grid but are excluded from R6/R7; no F1 cell -> G6 for the dependent predictions. F2/F2' cannot -> G6. F3 cannot -> R12 not_evaluable (no gate).
fallback_order: raise Y_hi to its §3.5.3 bound (lower of 300 PE median module charge and 0.95 median hit fraction)
F2: next a in {0.10, 0.20, 0.50}, then switch to F2' with b = 0.05, then 0.10

nuisance_policy.note: F3 per-PMT gains are part of the true mu but are not profiled: one free gain per PMT is an incidental-parameter block that would make every other factor's profiled information identically zero. The ceilings are lower bounds because profiling ignores the known yield/module-gain priors.
